{{short description|German physicist}}
'''Herbert Walther''' (January 19, 1935 in [[Ludwigshafen]], Germany – July 22, 2006 in [[Munich]]) was a leader in the fields of [[quantum optics]] and [[laser physics]]. He was a founding director of the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics]] (MPQ) in [[Garching]], [[Germany]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Ketterle, Wolfgang|authorlink=Wolfgang Ketterle|author2=Rempe, Gerhard|title=Obituary: Herbert Walther|journal=Physics Today|date=June 2007|volume=60|issue=6|pages=78–79|url=http://scitation.aip.org/content/aip/magazine/physicstoday/article/60/6/10.1063/1.2754618|doi=10.1063/1.2754618|bibcode = 2007PhT....60f..78K |doi-access=|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He also was Chair of Physics at [[LMU Munich]]. He is primarily known for his experimental work on cavity [[quantum electrodynamics]] (in the form of the [[micromaser]]) as well his groundbreaking work on the [[ion trap]].

At the time of his death he had over 600 publications and numerous awards from a number of prestigious physics and optics societies. In 1978, he won the [[Max Born Medal and Prize]]. In 1988, he received the [[Einstein Prize for Laser Science]], in 1990, he received the [[Charles Hard Townes Award]],<ref>[http://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/charlestownes/ Charles Hard Townes Award]</ref> in 1993 the [[Albert A. Michelson Medal]]<ref>[https://www.fi.edu/laureates/herbert-walther Albert A. Michelson Medal]</ref> from the [[Franklin Institute]] in [[Philadelphia]] and in 2003 the [[Frederic Ives Medal]] of The [[Optical Society]].<ref name=Ives>{{cite web| url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/ivesquinn/| title=Frederic Ives Medal / Jarus W. Quinn Prize| website=The Optical Society| access-date=7 October 2018}}</ref>
